description: `useRef(initial)` returns the same `{ current }` object on every render. Changing `current` does **not** re-render.
Data an event handler or effect needs across renders but the UI does not display, like a timer id or an `AbortController`.
`<input ref={inputRef} />` makes React set `inputRef.current` to the DOM node after commit and back to `null` on unmount.
Refs step outside React's data flow. Avoid reading or writing `ref.current` during render; use state for anything shown on screen.
